neet_phy_u10_t11_1.working: The beat frequency is the difference of the two frequencies: |260 - 256| = 4 beats per second.

neet_phy_u10_t11_2.working: The unknown fork is 384 ± 6, so it is 378 or 390 Hz. Wax lowers its frequency. If it were 390 Hz, lowering it moves it toward 384 Hz and the beats decrease, which matches. So the original frequency was 390 Hz.

neet_phy_u10_t11_3.working: The beat frequency is 504 - 498 = 6 Hz. The time between successive loudness maxima is the beat period, 1/6 s.

neet_phy_u10_t11_4.working: A: beats per second = |ν1 - ν2| (II). B: the tone heard is the average frequency, (ν1 + ν2)/2 (III). C: wax adds mass and lowers the frequency (IV). D: filing removes mass and raises the frequency (I).

neet_phy_u10_t11_5.working: A is true: beats are distinguishable only for a difference of about 10 Hz or less. B is true: the heard tone is 303 Hz with 6 beats per second. C is false: if wax increases the beats, the unknown fork had the lower frequency. D is true: beat period = 1/|ν1 - ν2|. E is false: filing raises the frequency. So A, B and D are correct.
